name: MCP9601 I2C thermocouple amplifier
description: Microchip thermocouple EMF-to-temperature converter with built-in cold-junction compensation and thermocouple open-circuit / short-circuit detection, reporting the thermocouple (hot-junction) temperature in 0.0625 °C steps over I2C; supports type K, J, T, N, S, E, B and R thermocouples (type K: -200 to 1372 °C). Runs on 2.7–5.5 V (chip). Sold as: Adafruit MCP9601 (MCP96L01) I2C Thermocouple Amplifier - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (product 5165; 9-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, A1, A2, A3, A4, ADDR, plus a 2-pin screw terminal for the thermocouple and two STEMMA QT sockets; MCP96L01 grade, ±2 °C typ / ±4 °C max), I2C address 0x67 (ADDR unconnected; 0x60 with ADDR to GND).
eli5: Plug a thermocouple wire into it and it tells your board how hot the tip is, even inside an oven or a flame, and warns you if the wire comes loose.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3.3–5 V (use the same voltage as your board's logic, 3.3 V on ESP32/Pico); feeds the chip directly

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10k pull-up to VIN on the board), 100 kHz

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10k pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Alert 1 output (push-pull, programmable), not needed for basic use

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Alert 2 output, not needed for basic use

pins.name: A3
pins.description: Alert 3 output, not needed for basic use

pins.name: A4
pins.description: Alert 4 output, not needed for basic use

pins.name: ADDR
pins.description: Address select: left unconnected = 0x67 (default); to GND = 0x60; back jumpers 43k = 0x66, 22k = 0x65

buildNotes: The thermocouple goes into the 2-pin screw terminal marked + and -, not the header (type K: yellow +, red -). If the reading falls when you heat the tip, swap the wires.
Read a temperature by writing the register pointer (0x00 = thermocouple, 0x02 = cold junction), then reading 2 bytes in a separate transaction; value = signed 16-bit × 0.0625 °C.
Set the thermocouple type in register 0x05 (bits 6-4: 0 = K, 1 = J, 2 = T, 3 = N, 4 = S, 5 = E, 6 = B, 7 = R) to match your probe, or the reading will be wrong.

STATUS register 0x04: bit 4 = thermocouple open (disconnected), bit 5 = thermocouple shorted to VDD/GND. The board already has the VSENSE resistors these need; ignore the temperature while either bit is set.
The chip stretches the I2C clock for up to 60 µs; use 100 kHz. Raspberry Pi (Linux) I2C does not handle clock stretching well, so lower its bus speed or use a microcontroller.
Default address 0x67 with ADDR unconnected; tie ADDR to GND for 0x60 when using two boards.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mcp9601 import MCP9601

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = MCP9601(i2c, tc_type='K')
while True:
    print('TH=%.2fC TC=%.2fC %s' % (sensor.temperature(), sensor.ambient(), sensor.fault()))
    time.sleep(1)
